summary: Lycurgus (Ancient Greek: Λυκοῦργος), son of Pronax and grandson of Talaus of Argos, is a Biantid prince and brother of Amphithea (wife of Adrastus). Apollodorus counts him among those Asclepius raised from the dead; Pausanias preserves his quarrel with Amphiaraus in Polygnotus' painting at Delphi.

sections.heading: Biantid of Argos
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 1.9.13) places Lycurgus among Pronax's children in the house of Talaus — uncle by marriage to the circle of the Seven against Thebes. One notice lists him among those Asclepius restored to life.
Pausanias (3.18.12) describes Polygnotus' underworld at Delphi: Amphiaraus and Lycurgus son of Pronax come to blows while Adrastus and Tydeus restrain them — the feud before the Theban march.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Distinct from Lycurgus of Arcadia (Tegea), Lycurgus of Nemea (father of Opheltes), the Thracian foe of Dionysus, and the Spartan lawgiver. The atlas id lycurgus-pronax is Pronax's Argive son alone.
